title: Software process models
subtitle: Building software is not just coding: a process decides what is built, in what order, and how surprises are handled.

sections.title: Why software engineering
sections.body: Software is complex, changes constantly and is invisible, so large projects fail for management reasons more often than technical ones: unclear requirements, poor estimates, weak testing. Software engineering applies systematic, measurable methods to develop, operate and maintain software. Key attributes of good software: maintainable, dependable, efficient, usable.

questions.prompt: Which attribute does most of the lifetime cost depend on?

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: Most software spends most of its life being changed.

sections.title: Waterfall
sections.body: Phases run in sequence: requirements → design → implementation → testing → deployment → maintenance, each signed off before the next. Good when requirements are stable and well understood (e.g. safety-critical specs). Weakness: a mistake found late is expensive, and the customer sees nothing until the end.

choices.text: Requirements are stable and well understood.

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: The plan can be fixed up front.

figures.caption: Figure 1.2.1 — waterfall
figures.note: The token flows one way; there is no loop back.

sections.title: Incremental and spiral
sections.body: Incremental: deliver working slices; each increment adds features and gets feedback. Spiral: each loop = plan → risk analysis → build prototype → evaluate; risk drives the next loop, so it suits large, uncertain projects. Prototyping builds a throw-away model to clarify requirements.

questions.prompt: The spiral model is driven by…

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: Each loop targets the biggest remaining risk.

figures.caption: Figure 1.3.1 — spiral
figures.note: Each trip around the loop reduces risk.

sections.title: Agile and Scrum
sections.body: The Agile manifesto values working software, customer collaboration and responding to change over plans and paperwork. Scrum: a product owner keeps a prioritised backlog; every 1–4 week sprint the team pulls items, holds a daily stand-up, delivers an increment, then runs a review and retrospective. XP adds practices: pair programming, test-first, continuous integration.

sections.title: Effort estimation: COCOMO
sections.body: Basic COCOMO (organic projects): effort E = 2.4·(KLOC)^1.05 person-months, development time T = 2.5·E^0.38 months. It is an estimate from size, so it is only as good as the size guess.

questions.prompt: Doubling code size in COCOMO (exponent 1.05) raises effort by…

problems.prompt: A 10 KLOC organic project. Find the effort.

sections.title: Choosing a process
sections.body:
SituationLean towards
Fixed, well-known requirementsWaterfall
Changing requirements, keen usersAgile / Scrum
Large, risky, novelSpiral
Need early feedback on UIPrototyping

questions.prompt: A start-up unsure what customers want should prefer…

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: Agile reduces the cost of being wrong.

responses.title: Close, but not it.
responses.body: It would be wrong by month two.
